name: 13_kv_cache_vs_cpu_temp
title: Race-to-idle effect: aggressive eviction can raise CPU temp via higher throughput
wave_finding: Wave-8 race-to-idle: smaller cache -> faster decode -> more sustained compute -> higher mean CPU temp

panels.linestyle: solid for cache, dashed for CPU temp

sensors.row_filter: 10 C < temp < 110 C (drop obvious bad reads, NaN-safe)

regression_global.model: cpu_C = a + b * n_kv_cells (per sensor sample, all policies)
regression_global.interpretation: Weak positive cross-policy correlation: cache size alone explains only ~2.5% of CPU-temp variance because the dominant driver is decode throughput (sustained compute), not cache footprint per se.

finding.headline: Race-to-idle effect: cells with smaller caches (K=256) decode faster (8.00 tok/s vs 7.11 tok/s for K=1024) and therefore keep the big cores at a higher mean temperature even though their KV footprint is smaller.
evidence: K=256 mean big-core CPU temp = 66.01 C  (decode 8.00 tok/s)
K=384 mean big-core CPU temp = 65.95 C  (decode 7.76 tok/s)
K=1024 mean big-core CPU temp = 64.85 C (decode 7.11 tok/s)
Same workload, same DVFS, same watchdog; only the eviction budget K differs.
finding.policy_implication: Aggressive eviction trades DRAM heat (lower KV footprint) for higher sustained CPU load -> the system gets hotter on the CPU side, not cooler. Must co-optimise CPU and DRAM thermals when choosing K.
